openingLines: An empty pantry makes for a quiet bar. What can I do for you?
People come here for a drink and a little news. Which are you after?
Pull up a chair. There is always something to talk about, even when supplies are short.

find-rope-thanks.text: That's the rope. Good. The cellar shelves are about one bad night away from collapsing. Here's what I promised.

greeting.text: Viktor Petrov. I run this bar, when there's anything left to run. Want a drink, a cigarette, or a story that'll make you wish you'd stayed home?

choices.text: [Quest] Tell Viktor that the records lead to the restricted factory warehouse.
[Quest] Any word on your missing supplies?
[Quest] Pavel says he informed the capital.
Do you believe Pavel reported the shortages?
[Quest] The letter is back in the postbox.
What do you really think of the quarantine?
Do you have a job for me?
[Work] Here are your food and alcohol.
[Courier] I am here to collect the parcel.
How long have you worked here?
What have you got to sell?
[Delivery] Deliver 1 Beer bottle to Viktor Petrov.
[Find item] Tell me about your request.
[Find item] I found the requested item.
What have you heard about the nights?
Can you tell me about a specific person?
[Quest] Did you know a guard with a key to the old service gate?

menu.text: There's always a little spirits behind the counter. Food and other drinks depend on what turns up each morning. Have a look. If you see something you like, buy it before somebody else does.

advice.text: When your head starts playing tricks on you, a shot of spirits can steady your nerves and restore Sanity. A smoke helps me too. Don't let your Sanity hit zero. And don't mistake a clear head for a safe street.

about.text: Been pouring drinks long enough to know when a man wants to talk and when he wants to forget. Soldiers come in for both. Morning, afternoon, evening: I'm at the bar in Center. At night, I'm in apartment 51 in Living District. Door locked, curtains shut. Usually.

cashier-1-cashier-1-deliver-0.text: A beer bottle. Now there's a sight worth celebrating. Thanks, I'll mark the delivery down.

courier-pickup-confirmed.text: Here's the parcel. The recipient's in your journal. Keep it dry, and don't stop to chat with patrols.

courier-delivery-thanks.text: You made it back. That's worth something these days. Here's your payment.

find-item-instructions.text: The item and recipient are in your journal. Find it, hand it over, and try not to attract attention.

find-item-payment.text: That's the one. Here's your payment. No questions, no paperwork.

supplies-job.text: I've got a job, if you're hungry enough for one. Bring me one food item and one alcoholic drink. Any kind. I'll give you 10 Thalers and a frying pan. Can't serve a bar full of frightened people with empty shelves.

supplies-accepted.text: One food item, one alcoholic drink. Bring them here when you've got both. And don't let anyone talk you into giving them away on the way.

supplies-thanks.text: Food and a bottle. Beautiful. Here's your 10 Thalers and the frying pan. More useful than half the promises coming out of the capital. I once knew a guard who carried a key to the old service gate.

choices.text: Tell me more about the missing guard.

town-opinion.text: The quarantine? Necessary, they say. Pills every day, doors locked every night. Sure. Maybe it'll all be over soon. That's what you wanted to hear, isn't it?

choices.text: [Intimidation] Drop the official line. What do you think?
[Diplomacy] I won’t repeat this. Tell me what you think.

town-dissatisfied.text: All right, you want the truth? We're being left to rot. I know Dusan thinks the pills are poison. I still take mine. If they do nothing, fine. If they help, even better. But I've heard gunfire after curfew, and I've served soldiers who couldn't hold a glass steady. Whatever's out there, it isn't going away.

shortages-offer.text: Look at those shelves. Soon I'll be serving boiled water and charging for the glass. Ask Zofia when the food and drink deliveries are coming. I'll pay you and throw in an enamel mug. At least the mug won't lie to us.

shortages-accepted.text: Zofia runs the shop. Ask when the next delivery's due. She hears things before I do, unless a soldier gets drunk enough to talk.

shortages-paid.text: So Pavel informed the capital. Wonderful. Perhaps they'll send us a framed acknowledgment to eat. Here's your payment and the enamel mug, as promised.

letter-offer.text: Pavel says he's told the capital everything. I'd like to see what 'everything' means in his handwriting. Check the postbox in Center at night. Find his letter and bring it to me. Then we'll put it back before he notices. Yes, I know what walks those streets after dark. I'm asking anyway.

choices.text: I will check the postbox at night.

letter-accepted.text: The postbox in Center. After dark. Bring me Pavel's letter before returning it. If you hear something calling from the far end of the street, don't go looking for its owner.

letter-read.text: Listen to this: 'There are no problems in the town. Everything is under control.' Not a word about empty shelves or the people who never came home. Put it back in the same postbox at night. I want him to keep believing nobody's read it.

letter-paid.text: Good. Pavel's letter is back where it belongs, and we know what his promises are worth. Here's your payment and the barbed bat. Keep it close after sundown.

ask-about.text: You want to know what's happening in this town? Fine. Just don't repeat my name when you repeat the stories.

choices.text: [Barter] What makes those noises outside at night?
[Diplomacy] What have the soldiers told you about hallucinations?
[Barter] Why does the factory need so much ammunition?
[Intimidation] What happened to the patrol near the factory?
[Diplomacy] Have you ever seen one of those things yourself?
Why would a guard carry a maintenance key?

ask-about-answer-1.text: Every night I hear something dragging along the street. Slow, heavy, like a loaded cart with one broken wheel. Then comes a scraping sound against the walls. The official explanation is pipes, stray dogs, or a sick mind. Funny how the pipes stop whenever the patrols start shooting.

ask-about-answer-2.text: Soldiers drink here when they're off duty. One swore he saw a woman standing under a streetlamp, facing the wrong way. When he called out, she turned without moving her feet. His friend said it was the pills, or exhaustion. Then they both went quiet when I asked why they'd fired half a magazine at her. Nadia would call it a stress reaction. Maybe she is right about the fear. That still does not explain the ammunition.

ask-about-answer-3.text: The soldiers get food, ammunition, fuel, fresh lamps. We get ration slips. I don't begrudge a hungry man his supper, but why are they hauling crates of ammunition toward the factory every night? Dusan says something big is kept there. I told him to stop drinking his own moonshine. Then I heard the factory siren go off after midnight. Irina is trying to keep the factory running while Pavel counts crates that never seem to reach her. That is a joke without a punchline.

ask-about-answer-4.text: A sergeant came in with his sleeve torn from shoulder to wrist. Said he'd caught it on a fence. Another soldier laughed, then started crying. They'd been posted near the factory. I asked what happened. The sergeant grabbed my arm and said, 'If the searchlights go out, don't look up.' Next morning, he was gone. Transferred, they told me.

ask-about-answer-5.text: You want to know what I believe? I think there are things outside after dark that no fever invented. I've seen a shape cross the street where there wasn't room for a man to pass, and I've heard something breathe outside my window on the fifth floor. I take the pills anyway. Dusan calls me a fool. Maybe I am. But the soldiers have guns, the government has secrets, and I have a bottle. Guess which one helps me sleep. Milena came asking whether the men at my bar knew anything about her father. I could not give her an answer. I gave her tea instead. Even I know when not to offer a drink.

people-menu.text: People talk after a drink. Does not mean I believe every word.

people-about-elena-jovanovic.text: Elena comes in for news, never a drink. Funny how she remembers every complaint word for word. I serve her tea and make sure my customers know when she's listening.

people-about-pavel-sokolov.text: Sokolov? He files reports, I collect empty glasses. We both know how to make a bad night disappear on paper. Difference is, I don't pretend the glasses were never broken.

people-about-dusan-markovic.text: Dusan's my friend. Loud, stubborn bastard. He tells me to stop taking the pills; I tell him to stop drinking my profits. Neither of us listens. At least he knows what he's seen.

people-about-irina-kovalenko.text: Irina keeps the factory standing with string and stubbornness. She pays her tabs, even when I tell her not to. If she says something's wrong with those doors, I'd listen.

people-about-zofia-nowak.text: Zofia's got an answer for every empty shelf: 'The capital is handling it.' I'd like to order a crate of that confidence. Probably out of stock.

people-about-milena-vukovic.text: Milena reminds me of people who still think the truth fixes things. I hope she's right. I also hope she learns when to lower her voice before someone teaches her the hard way.

people-about-nadia-morozova.text: Nadia patches up men who swear they fell down stairs. Some of those stairs must have teeth. She never laughs at that joke. Can't say I blame her.

story-official-seal-viktor.text: So the paperwork leads back to that warehouse. That tells us who signed for supplies, not what happened to the patients.

postman-thanks.text: Thank you for bringing my letter.

escape-guard-key-account.text: I knew a guard who carried the old service-gate key on his belt; he took the factory night watch and never came back.

choices.text: Why would a guard carry a maintenance key?

escape-guard-key-lore-answer.text: The service gate predates the quarantine. Shift guards kept maintenance routes open, but the new orders sealed everything without recalling the old keys. A lock can outlast the authority that issued it.
